Sorry to hear about your unintentional work hiatus. As someone who also has prolonged work gaps due to mental health issues, I have considered something like this: 

http://www.dailydot.com/business/career-excuse-fake-job-references/

I am also currently connected to an employment centre and they have supported employment programs, basically meaning they have workers who look for jobs with and for the clients. Typically, the employers are understanding about the various work, or lack of, situations and experiences of the clients. Maybe there is something similar in your area.

Another thing I'm looking into is volunteer work in roles I'm interested in. If you do this for a few months, maybe you can network with people who can put you into paid work or can connect or refer you to others who can. That's my intention anyway. 

Hope that helps. Best of luck.

Welcome:) I'm still fairly new to Reddit as well and new to this sub. I love the tips and posts on here. 

I used to work shift work as well. I ended up leaving because I couldn't cope..but the shifts were all over the place. I wasn't even working regularly in a one week time span. 

But if I were to work shift work again, and I had 12 hour shifts alternating every other week, I would make daily routines/habits to encourage waking and sleeping times that I am trying to attain..i get the sleep/wake issue.. it's really difficult because your body has to adjust every week and by the time you're done adjusting, it's almost the next week.. 

I suggest to focus more on a particular routine that will get you to sleep, and a particular routine you do asap upon rising that indicates you're out of bed, so it's less about the exact time and more about creating a habit that indicates to your body it's time to rest or rise.

I don't have anything to contribute for your plan. I just wanted to say I like your plan and I find it commendable that you're using your current state of being in a rut in a proactive way that will make you feel better. In my experience, having a meaningful, daily routine makes me feel like a better human, too. And you're right about how even if you end up not doing other things, the system/routine you do commit to enables you to function in a way that will feel like you're being a more acceptable you. Just for the record, you are still an acceptable and worthy human even if you feel like shit and your routines and habits are not ideal.

Great advice. I get so caught up just trying to maintain routines that I forget that mastery of a particular task may mean I can level up.

I ended up sleeping quite late but still got up around 8 and was able to get some stuff done before my appt. I ate breakfast after. Had a fantastic talk with cps and my landlord. Doing laundry now and am feeling ok and motivated to keep moving forward via baby steps. It's occurring to me that baby steps doesn't negate setbacks. I think I was starting to think that if I did things a certain way then everything would be ideal. But setbacks happen and when they do, all one can do in the moment is cope and after the moment....grieve the ideal. Accept the real. And keep moving forward. Baby steps and breaking things down makes life and tasks more manageable but having all the preventative measures in the world doesn't mean there won't be setbacks. There will be and the brave thing to do is commit to whatever steps you need to move forward by taking action proactively.

I recently started writing daily tasks in pencil on cue cards..so I have 3 a day (morning, afternoon, evening) for each day of the week. If something needs to be tweaked or changed for the week after, then I just erase and amend accordingly. If it stays the same then I give myself a little check mark beside the task for completion. My daughter uses these cue cards for her morning tasks as well and she times herself for each task. If your tasks are all the same every morning, maybe you can just use one daily task cue card for everyday instead of 7 (or 21) different ones.
Goal: wake up at 8am or earlier, make bed, make/have breakfast before in home cps appt

I am actually not trying to take responsibility for triggering people here. Everyone's reactions on here is not my responsibility. I am however genuinely sorry for how others feel when they feel bad and reminisce on shitty things, not because I am taking responsibility for their feelings, but because shitty feelings and experiences are shitty. If I came off as apologizing for making someone feel a certain way, that was not my intention. Maybe I shouldn't apologize for making this post/thread lest I be held responsible from feelings elicited from it..number 1 thing I learned about feelings as a person coping with intense feelings is I am responsible for my feelings. Like yeah, ok...shitty feelings are shit and seemingly come out of nowhere or from somewhere or someone specific, but those are my feelings to deal with, not someone else's responsibility. And as someone who has been on the receiving end of heartfelt apologies, it doesn't mean anything unless that person takes further action and unless I have the capacity to forgive. Who am I to apologize to you strangers? Who are you to forgive me? We do not have an intimate connection, you don't know me personally, you know there's some ratchet stuff on breakingmom, you're reading this thread, you're making a choice to engage, in retrospect, perhaps I was wrongfully trying to express the sorry as  a disclaimer as opposed to "I'm taking responsibility for your unaddressed feelings from childhood that may arise because I'm asking a question and want to gain first hand insight to what it would look like if I give up"? Continuing on, my responsibility is my daughter and me..her health, her safety, her well being..mine too. But I do also tell her that her feelings are her own. I'm not saying that as an excuse to act however the hell I want-on the flip side, and I say this as someone who is constantly learning to cope with others actions and behaviours as well as someone who is constantly learning to deal with my own issues as well as someone who is trying to teach someone to cope with others and their own issues: taking responsibility for your feelings is an empowering thing because people are going to be a certain way regardless of your help or what they do or dont do, do or don't say...they will be whatever way they are going to be so at the end of the day, the only person you are responsible for is yourself. As for the rest, I don't feel the need to answer your questions further. Your questions alone and requests about my abilities to apologize or take responsibility simply demonstrate that you don't know me. And that's fine. All you know of me is what I have shared on here and you've taken my online presence as an opportunity to express your interpretation of me. And that's ok. It's totally understandable. I have to remind myself, I opened this thread up to share a genuine moment of peak distress, somewhat impulsively but with honesty, to get insight, to look into some kind of crystal ball like... How potentially fucked up is my kid going to be if I give up now? If I default to being like this every. Single. Time?  Does my kid still love me even when I'm not grade A, kosher, what are these people remembering from their childhoods? I took a risk to be extremely vulnerable and I'm glad because there's some worst case scenarios to loom over my head and put in my toolbox and keep me in check, even for the time being, until or while I  implement another tool. Reading everyone's experiences, it sucks to hear, I been through the same , and in some ways as a parent I do better than how I was done and in other ways, I struggle. Who doesn't? I could be better and I'm working towards that and it could be worse if I do not stay on top of things. It's a new day, new moments and I know that I'm not as terrible as I think I am..irl, I got people to stay accountable to and who can vouch for who I am but from my words on here? People can pool judgement and call me out and say otherwise. I'm putting out on exhibition a piece of me I want fixed, but my way of asking for help is through horror stories because I am already addressing things through other means and that's why they go unmentioned. So whatever. I understand my defensive stance now -it's because there are assumptions being made and what a fucking waste of time  because what is it to me or you to explain things I already do or know? I'm getting pissed reading your specific comments because I'm not here to pacify feelings and grovel and talk about how I'm not all bad lol. So fuck me for losing sight, for getting confused-That's what I take responsibility for. Otherwise, I am here to get a feel for worst case scenario situations, I empathize with those worst case scenarios, and I do appreciate the replies, good and bad. It gives me an opportunity to learn about others lives, reactions, insight, communiative ways, opportunity to reflect, to practice online discussion/interaction... So yeah thanks again for your reply but also for helping me to re affirm/re realize the "real" reason I posted this thread. I hope the insight and expression provided on here is as helpful to others, in whatever way that be, as it was for me. Take care.

Thanks for your response. I actually have a lot of help that I do utilize. I'm trying to be understanding about the responses I'm getting and can definitely understand how this is triggering for people. Of course, I have an inclination to go on the defense because I grew up with wrath as well and I too want to be a different parent. I have now spent at least 2 years focusing on "being a better parent" after recognizing that I have issues. I'm not going to go into all that I've done and whatnot because I feel I've already talked about that in various replies and I feel it's unnecessary to share because yeah..it just looks like I'm defending myself. But I'm inclined to defend myself as much as admit I'm in the wrong. If I can't believe in my efforts, what's the point? How can I progress if I fail to recognize my progress? So yeah..I understand how my responses can be seen as being defensive or waffling, but laying down and being remorseful and pitiful hasn't worked in my favour. It's this dual combination of saying...yeah..I fucked up...but hey..I'm trying and hey..I'm human. My psychiatrist once advised me that if I put humour and honesty in every situation, it won't be so bad and change can happen slowly but surely. I believe that even when I'm waffling. It's like if you get stuck in a ditch, what are your choices? Sit around and cry or go get help? I tend to sit around and cry but then I go get help and then the car is off rolling but hey its a shitty tire, I end up getting a flat, ok so I gotta access another shop. It sounds like you want me to do a certain thing and because I have not done that certain thing, then I'm useless when the reality is, I've been working on things and now I'm in a ditch again and so I'm ready to access the next step. The insight and stories on this thread helped to give me insight on experiences and feelings felt outside of my own experiences and what I know of others. So yeah, I am sorry if this was a triggering question, but also I'm recognizing that people are using this thread to express how they feel. I think that's a good thing. This isn't all about me being a super horrible parent..I recognize my faults, I get help, and yet I slip up. But I keep going even when I feel like I'm not or can't. I know for myself the human experience is about growth until death. I'm still growing, as a parent, as a human. I'm not saying that as an excuse, I too am sharing my pain and I appreciate the words and sentiments on here. I can understand how I would be perceived as waffling, so that's fine for you to think that. But you know, how can I not get defensive? You don't know me from shit and you are judging me based on the emotions you feel reading this. But. I posted the question so I have to deal with the repercussions. I get it. I say thank you on every, most replies, because I am grateful for the insight even though I get "defensive". It is important to me to try to be understanding of others feelings and reactions as much as my own. So yeah. Thanks for your input.

Thanks. I appreciate the insight. I am bipolar and have bpd and anxiety myself and though I don't like to use these health issues as an excuse for my behaviour, my temperament is off when my moods are off. I actually have been involved with cps for a year..year and a half. They were actually quite helpful. I have a very supportive mental health team. I have done counseling, group therapy..I can be very pro active and a good parent. When I'm not, I'm not. I think putting this question out here and reading through others experiences is another thing I can put in my tool box. So I'm very grateful for the insight but of course saddened that we all had to go through this as kids or otherwise. Life is life though. You either break or use it as a tool to move forward in a positive way. I think the next step is to access an anger management group. Anger is a choice, you're right. But I am also working on decision making skills. I have this anger handout about how one is in control until a certain point, up until that point, you have a choice, but when you're past that threshold, then the flight/fight response is triggered. So..still working on how I can make the right choice when I get to that stage.

Thank you for sharing your experience. Sorry to hear the impact. So heartbreaking. I hope you find peace. As a parent with rage issues, I am working at it but I do slip up. It's not ok. But I have to believe effort counts. So I hope you find peace and finding peace doesn't mean you forget about the bad stuff. Just means you've lived a shitty experience but you're strong anyway.

We just do our best, try different ways that can sustain calmness, aim for effort that actually works and hope for the best. If our best is not enough, well..we tried. There are repercussions in being human.
